name: QuaRot: Outlier-Free 4-Bit Inference in Rotated LLMs
problem: Activation outliers in LLMs make W4A4 (and even KV4) quantization collapse, and every fix so far keeps a handful of channels in higher precision.
mechanism: Computational invariance: inserting an orthogonal matrix Q into the residual stream is a no-op at full precision because Q^T Q = I, and any residual is orthogonal to itself, so the model output is unchanged while the outlier structure is redistributed across channels. QuaRot applies randomized Hadamard rotations end-to-end - to the embedding output, to the residual write/read paths, to the Q/K head inputs, and to the KV cache - so that all matmuls (weights, activations AND KV cache) can run in 4 bits with NO channel retained in higher precision.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract, LLaMA2-70B, 4-bit weights + activations + KV cache): at most 0.47 WikiText-2 perplexity loss and 99% of zero-shot performance retained. COMPRESSION RATIO: 4 bits on all three tensors, i.e. ~4x weight and ~4x KV-cache reduction vs FP16 (8x if counting weights+activations together). Also claims LOSSLESS 6-bit and 8-bit LLaMA2 with round-to-nearest and NO calibration data at all. This 0.47-ppl figure is the single most-cited number in the 4-bit LLM quantization literature and it is the paper's own, on one model family.
